findings.statement: SCARB1 is the top-ranked target, but its single-cell attribution does not hold across datasets: the dominant group is myeloid in the first dataset and tumour (RCC) in the second, with tumour-cell shares of [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] and [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. Part of the bulk signal may therefore come from myeloid cells rather than tumour cells.

SCARB1 protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory DIA cohort and replicates (log2 fold change [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334]).

CA9 is a surface protein and a known target (control), but the GTEx proteome flags it as enriched in a vital organ (stomach, tissue-specificity score [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19]) with high stomach staining; in the weakest quarter of donors only [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%] of tumour cells express it. This is a safety and heterogeneity caveat, not proof that a conjugate fails.

CD70 is a surface protein with no vital-organ proteome enrichment (maximum tissue-specificity score [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=0.34]), but immunohistochemistry staining data were not available, and only [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%] of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors. Proteome absence is not proof of absence in normal tissue.

SLC16A3 protein increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort (log2 fold change [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551]) and its one measured phosphosite also replicates.

NNMT protein increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort with many matched pairs (log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]); judge direction and significance, not size.

NNMT is attributed to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with tumour-versus-proximal-tubule log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=9.132] in the first and [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=5.573] in the second (only a few paired donors in the second).

NNMT is not a subgroup target candidate: mutant-versus-wild-type differences for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 and SETD2 are not significant in the CPTAC and TCGA comparisons, and the ccB minus ccA difference is not significant, so it would be relevant across genetic subgroups rather than one.

HK2 protein increase does not replicate: in the confirmatory DIA cohort the log2 fold change is [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256] with adjusted p-value [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074], despite a strong discovery change. Its top-10 target rank rests on RNA and discovery protein only.

PPP1R1A protein loss does not replicate: the confirmatory adjusted p-value is [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17], although the direction is the same and few matched pairs were available there. This is a weakness for a top-5 biomarker candidate; the one measured phosphosite does replicate.

PSAT1 protein loss in tumours replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]), but its one discovery phosphosite did not replicate.

PSAT1 differs by molecular subtype: the CPTAC protein ccB minus ccA difference is [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.cptac_protein.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=0.541], higher in ccB, and BAP1 mutants have higher RNA in CPTAC and TCGA but not protein, so it is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate.

PCK1 is not associated with a differential benefit between atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and sunitinib (difference adjusted p-value [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.769]); no arm-specific signal either, so PCK1 is a diagnostic or prognostic lead only, not a treatment-selection marker.

PCK1 protein loss replicates strongly in the confirmatory DIA cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]) and both measured phosphosites replicate.

CA9 expression is associated with, but does not separate, outcomes between the atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and sunitinib arms (difference adjusted p-value [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]); in the sunitinib arm the log hazard ratio per SD is [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336] (longer benefit with higher expression), not significant. The nivolumab-versus-everolimus difference is also not significant.

CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup target candidate (higher in mutants in CPTAC RNA and TCGA; TCGA RNA mutant minus wild-type log2 difference [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148]), but the CPTAC protein difference is only borderline, and it is lower in ccB than ccA.

CA9 has the same dominant cell group (tumour cells) in both single-cell datasets, so its attribution holds. The protein was not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort (too few matched pairs), which is missing data and not a failed replication.

CD70 has a large immune-cell component: immune cells make a share of its tumour transcripts of [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and it correlates positively with CD8 T cells; its log hazard ratio on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383]. Tumour-cell expression of CD70 therefore cannot be separated from immune expression in bulk data. It was also not tested in the confirmatory protein cohort.

FCGR3A, high in both rankings, is a microenvironment signal rather than a tumour target: immune cells make [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] of its tumour transcripts and the tumour-cell share in the first single-cell dataset is [gene=FCGR3A; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.000837], with myeloid as dominant group in both datasets.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is not associated with a differential benefit between nivolumab and everolimus (difference adjusted p-value [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]); no IMmotion150 arms were returned for it, so no statement can be made on the atezolizumab combination.

SLC16A3 is not associated with a differential benefit between nivolumab and everolimus (adjusted p-value [gene=SLC16A3; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]); higher expression is associated with earlier progression in the nivolumab arm but without significance.

ALDH6A1 protein loss replicates strongly in the confirmatory DIA cohort (log2 fold change [gene=ALDH6A1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.773]), supporting its biomarker rank.

ANGPTL4 protein increase replicates but weakly (confirmatory log2 fold change [gene=ANGPTL4; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=0.788], smaller than in discovery), so the effect is modest in the second cohort.

caveats: No gene differs between trial arms after correction; all treatment statements are associations and single-gene leads, not predictions.
CD70, CA9, FABP6 and DUSP9 were not tested in the confirmatory cohort (too few matched pairs); this is missing data, not a failed replication.
A high ADC score does not show a conjugate would work; CD70 staining data were missing; GTEx proteome absence is not proof of absence.
Replication in the confirmatory cohort covers the protein only and uses a different technology, so fold changes are not comparable in size.
Second single-cell dataset has only a few paired donors.

Other top-10 genes (VWF, SLPI, L1CAM, SLC6A19, CYP2J2, ENPP3) replicated at protein level in the confirmatory cohort but have no separate finding. EPAS1 and NNMT treatment records lack IMmotion150 arms.
